per_query.question: What products are most urgently at risk of stock-outs right now?
per_query.candidate_sql:
SELECT product_name, units_in_stock, reorder_level, (units_in_stock - reorder_level) AS stock_gap
FROM public.products
WHERE units_in_stock <= reorder_level
ORDER BY stock_gap ASC, units_in_stock ASC
per_query.reference_sql:
SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.units_in_stock, p.reorder_level
FROM public.products p
WHERE p.units_in_stock < p.reorder_level
ORDER BY (p.reorder_level - p.units_in_stock) DESC, p.product_id
LIMIT 5

per_query.question: How has revenue trended month by month after discounts?
per_query.candidate_sql:
SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) AS month, 
       SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS revenue_after_discount
FROM public.order_details od
JOIN public.orders o ON od.order_id = o.order_id
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month;
per_query.reference_sql:
SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)::date AS month,
       SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS revenue
FROM public.orders o
JOIN public.order_details od ON od.order_id = o.order_id
GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)::date
ORDER BY month

per_query.question: Which product categories actually generate the most revenue once discounts are considered?
per_query.candidate_sql:
SELECT c.category_name, SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS total_revenue
FROM public.order_details od
JOIN public.products p ON od.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN public.categories c ON p.category_id = c.category_id
GROUP BY c.category_name
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
LIMIT 5;
per_query.reference_sql:
SELECT c.category_name,
       SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS total_revenue
FROM public.categories c
JOIN public.products p ON p.category_id = c.category_id
JOIN public.order_details od ON od.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY c.category_name
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC, c.category_name

per_query.question: Which customers order unusually often, and roughly how much business do they represent for us?
per_query.candidate_sql:
SELECT c.company_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.freight) AS total_business
FROM public.orders o
JOIN public.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.company_name
HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM (SELECT COUNT(order_id) AS order_count FROM public.orders GROUP BY customer_id) AS subquery)
ORDER BY order_count DESC, total_business DESC
LIMIT 5;
per_query.reference_sql:
SELECT c.customer_id,
       c.company_name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count,
       SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity) AS total_order_value
FROM public.customers c
JOIN public.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN public.order_details od ON od.order_id = o.order_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.company_name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) > 10
ORDER BY total_order_value DESC, c.customer_id

per_query.question: Which shipping providers are causing delay issues, and what is their shipment volume?
per_query.candidate_sql:
SELECT ship_via, COUNT(order_id) AS shipment_volume, SUM(CASE WHEN shipped_date > required_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS delay_count
FROM public.orders
GROUP BY ship_via
ORDER BY delay_count DESC
per_query.reference_sql:
SELECT s.shipper_id,
       s.company_name,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.shipped_date > o.required_date) AS late_shipments,
       COUNT(*) AS total_shipments
FROM public.orders o
JOIN public.shippers s ON s.shipper_id = o.ship_via
GROUP BY s.shipper_id, s.company_name
ORDER BY late_shipments DESC, total_shipments DESC, s.shipper_id

per_query.question: Which employees drive the most sales revenue after discounts?
per_query.candidate_sql:
SELECT e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS total_revenue
FROM public.employees e
JOIN public.orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id
JOIN public.order_details od ON o.order_id = od.order_id
GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
LIMIT 5;
per_query.reference_sql:
SELECT e.employee_id,
       e.first_name,
       e.last_name,
       SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS total_revenue
FROM public.employees e
JOIN public.orders o ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id
JOIN public.order_details od ON od.order_id = o.order_id
GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC, e.employee_id

per_query.question: What are our top-selling products by quantity?
per_query.candidate_sql:
SELECT p.product_name, SUM(od.quantity) AS total_quantity
FROM public.products p
JOIN public.order_details od ON p.product_id = od.product_id
GROUP BY p.product_name
ORDER BY total_quantity DESC
LIMIT 5;
per_query.reference_sql:
SELECT p.product_id,
       p.product_name,
       SUM(od.quantity) AS quantity_sold
FROM public.products p
JOIN public.order_details od ON od.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name
ORDER BY quantity_sold DESC, p.product_id
LIMIT 5

per_query.question: Which suppliers tend to appear together in the same customer orders most often?
per_query.candidate_sql:
SELECT s1.company_name AS supplier1, s2.company_name AS supplier2, COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM public.order_details od1
JOIN public.products p1 ON od1.product_id = p1.product_id
JOIN public.suppliers s1 ON p1.supplier_id = s1.supplier_id
JOIN public.order_details od2 ON od1.order_id = od2.order_id AND od1.product_id <> od2.product_id
JOIN public.products p2 ON od2.product_id = p2.product_id
JOIN public.suppliers s2 ON p2.supplier_id = s2.supplier_id
WHERE s1.supplier_id < s2.supplier_id
GROUP BY s1.company_name, s2.company_name
ORDER BY order_count DESC
LIMIT 5;
per_query.reference_sql:
WITH order_suppliers AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT od.order_id, p.supplier_id
    FROM public.order_details od
    JOIN public.products p ON p.product_id = od.product_id
),
supplier_pairs AS (
    SELECT os1.supplier_id AS supplier_id_1,
           os2.supplier_id AS supplier_id_2,
           COUNT(*) AS co_order_count
    FROM order_suppliers os1
    JOIN order_suppliers os2
      ON os1.order_id = os2.order_id
     AND os1.supplier_id < os2.supplier_id
    GROUP BY os1.supplier_id, os2.supplier_id
)
SELECT s1.company_name AS supplier_1,
       s2.company_name AS supplier_2,
       sp.co_order_count
FROM supplier_pairs sp
JOIN public.suppliers s1 ON s1.supplier_id = sp.supplier_id_1
JOIN public.suppliers s2 ON s2.supplier_id = sp.supplier_id_2
ORDER BY sp.co_order_count DESC, supplier_1, supplier_2
LIMIT 10

per_query.question: How does average order value differ across customer countries?
per_query.candidate_sql:
SELECT c.country, AVG(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS average_order_value
FROM public.orders o
JOIN public.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN public.order_details od ON o.order_id = od.order_id
GROUP BY c.country
ORDER BY average_order_value DESC;
per_query.reference_sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
    SELECT o.order_id,
           c.country,
           SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS order_total
    FROM public.orders o
    JOIN public.customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    JOIN public.order_details od ON od.order_id = o.order_id
    GROUP BY o.order_id, c.country
)
SELECT country,
       AVG(order_total) AS avg_order_value
FROM order_totals
GROUP BY country
ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC, country

per_query.question: How many orders are still unshipped, and what are they worth after discounts?
per_query.candidate_sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS unshipped_orders_count, 
       SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS total_value_after_discounts
FROM public.orders o
JOIN public.order_details od ON o.order_id = od.order_id
WHERE o.shipped_date IS NULL;
per_query.reference_sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS pending_orders,
       SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS total_value
FROM public.orders o
JOIN public.order_details od ON od.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.shipped_date IS NULL
